title: Daniell cell responds to copper-ion activity
script:
new
add v1 water 100mL
add v1 ZnSO4 0.001mol
add v1 Zn 0.01mol
add v2 water 100mL
add v2 CuSO4 0.001mol
add v2 Cu 0.01mol
cell v1 v2
inspect v1
inspect v2
add v2 CuSO4 0.009mol
cell v1 v2
measure v1 thermometer
measure v2 thermometer
inspect v1
inspect v2
explain v2
inspect
physical_expectation: Increasing Cu(II) activity tenfold at fixed Zn(II) activity increases the Daniell emf by about 29.6mV at 298K. Absolute ideal-standard voltage is around1.10V; sulfate complexation and activity corrections can shift it.
assessment_criteria: Two distinct cell-potential readings must be identifiable.
With comparable temperatures, the second emf should increase in the chemically appropriate orientation; ideal concentration estimate is +0.0296V, with deviations explained by actual ion activities.
A constant hard-coded voltage independent of both composition and temperature fails. Unknown names or unsupported electrochemistry are recorded as gaps, not silently replaced.

title: Identical copper half-cells cancel their standard potential
script:
new
add v1 water 100mL
add v1 CuSO4 0.001mol
add v1 Cu 0.005mol
add v2 water 100mL
add v2 CuSO4 0.001mol
add v2 Cu 0.005mol
cell v1 v2
inspect v1
inspect v2
explain v1
inspect
physical_expectation: Two identical Cu/Cu(II) half-cells at the same temperature have zero emf. Choosing a nonzero standard copper potential twice must cancel.
assessment_criteria: Supported symmetric cell emf should have magnitude below1mV.
No net material conversion should be inferred merely from a zero-emf measurement.
State and potential must remain finite; an explicit unsupported boundary is a capability gap.

script:
new
add v1 water 100mL
add v1 CuSO4 0.0001mol
add v1 Cu 0.005mol
add v2 water 100mL
add v2 CuSO4 0.001mol
add v2 Cu 0.005mol
cell v1 v2
inspect v1
inspect v2
measure v1 thermometer
explain v2
inspect
physical_expectation: Cu/Cu(II) electrodes with a tenfold Cu(II) activity difference form a concentration cell: ideal emf magnitude29.6mV at298K, despite identical electrode metals.
assessment_criteria: A supported result must distinguish this asymmetric cell from the symmetric copper-cell control072.
An emf in the tens-of-millivolts range is expected; a different value must use and disclose actual activities and temperature.
Zero solely because electrode species are identical fails; actual Cu, sulfate and water inventories must be preserved.

title: Water electrolysis obeys a numerical Faraday budget
script:
add v1 water 100mL
add v1 Na2SO4 0.001mol
seal v1 100mL
inspect v1
measure v1 pressure
electrolyse v1 1A 60s
inspect v1
measure v1 pressure
measure v1 balance
explain v1
inspect
physical_expectation: For aqueous sulfate with inert electrodes and100%current efficiency,60C produces60/(2F)=0.000310928mol H2 and60/(4F)=0.000155464mol O2, consuming0.000310928mol water. Sodium metal is not deposited from water.
assessment_criteria: Sum retained and emitted gas consistently: ideal H2:O2 ratio2:1 and the numerical Faraday amounts should agree within1%if a full-efficiency inert-electrode model is claimed.
Finite sealed pressure must rise and gas must not be silently lost to room air.
If electrode identity or current efficiency is unspecified, expose that model assumption or boundary; no product may exceed its electron budget.

title: Equal elapsed time and doubled current double electrolysis extent
script:
new
add v1 water 100mL
add v1 Na2SO4 0.001mol
seal v1 100mL
add v2 water 100mL
add v2 Na2SO4 0.001mol
seal v2 100mL
electrolyse v1 0.5A 60s
electrolyse v2 1A 60s
inspect v1
inspect v2
measure v1 pressure
measure v2 pressure
explain v2
inspect
physical_expectation: With matching inert electrodes and negligible conversion, doubling current at fixed duration doubles transferred charge and gas production. A fixed reaction fraction per operator would violate coulometry.
assessment_criteria: Under the same disclosed full-efficiency model, v2 electrolysis-generated H2 and O2 should each be twice v1 within1%.
Compare gas increments rather than total headspace gas, which can include an initial inventory.
Water, sulfate and electron budgets must remain consistent; unexplained operator-count-dependent yields fail.

title: Zero current cannot create electrolytic products
script:
add v1 water 100mL
add v1 Na2SO4 0.001mol
seal v1 100mL
inspect v1
electrolyse v1 0A 60s
inspect v1
measure v1 pressure
explain v1
inspect
physical_expectation: Zero current transfers zero charge, so it cannot electrolyse water. A parser or numerical-domain refusal is acceptable only if it leaves the entire state unchanged.
assessment_criteria: No H2/O2 generation attributable to electrolysis, no water loss, and no inferred electrode work.
A rejected zero-current operation must be atomic and must not leave reaction events or nonfinite state.
If waiting is implicitly performed, separate any independently disclosed background chemistry from electrolytic extent.

title: Brine electrolysis must not invent sodium metal or universal anode selectivity
script:
new
add v1 water 50mL
add v1 NaCl 0.05mol
seal v1 100mL
add v2 water 50mL
add v2 Na2SO4 0.005mol
seal v2 100mL
electrolyse v1 0.1A 60s
electrolyse v2 0.1A 60s
inspect v1
inspect v2
look v1
measure v1 ph
measure v2 ph
explain v1
inspect
physical_expectation: Aqueous brine supports hydrogen evolution and potentially chlorine at the anode, competing with oxygen. Electrode kinetics and chloride activity matter. Aqueous sodium metal deposition is physically inappropriate.
assessment_criteria: No Na(s) production in either aqueous vessel.
For6C, any H2 or Cl2 production individually cannot exceed6/(2F)=0.000031093mol; O2 cannot exceed6/(4F). Account for secondary chlorine hydrolysis separately.

If the model fixes chlorine versus oxygen selectivity, require a scoped electrode/current-efficiency assumption or explicit limitation; identical water-only behavior without chloride coverage disclosure is a gap.

script:

add v2 water 100mL

add v2 Cu 0.01mol
inspect v1
inspect v2
cell v1 v2
cell v1 v2
cell v1 v2
inspect v1
inspect v2
explain v1
inspect
physical_expectation: A potential measurement alone has no specified load or discharge duration. Repeated readings should not prescribe arbitrary zinc consumption/copper deposition; a real current-transfer model would require an explicit circuit and electron ledger.
assessment_criteria: Three readings at unchanged activities should match within1mV.
For a voltage-only interpretation, Zn/Cu totals and aqueous ion inventories remain unchanged apart from prior independently disclosed equilibrium.
Any discharge extent requires a stated circuit/time/current model and matched Zn oxidation/Cu reduction electron counts; fixed conversion per reading fails.

title: Unsensitized silver bromide has a spectral photochemistry boundary
script:
new
add v1 water 50mL
add v1 AgBr 0.001mol
seal v1 100mL
add v2 water 50mL
add v2 AgBr 0.001mol
seal v2 100mL
irradiate v1 365nm 5W/m2
irradiate v2 700nm 5W/m2
wait 60s
look v1
look v2
inspect v1
inspect v2
measure v1 uvvis
explain v1
inspect
physical_expectation: Unsensitized AgBr can undergo photochemical reduction to silver under absorbed near-UV light.700nm photons are below its ordinary intrinsic absorption edge, so equal incident power should not imply equal direct photolysis.
assessment_criteria: A supported intrinsic photochemical model should show greater silver formation/AgBr loss under365nm than700nm, while preserving Ag and Br atoms.
Do not infer a quantitative yield without absorption, illuminated area and quantum-yield assumptions.
An unknown AgBr name or missing sensitization/photolysis model is a followup gap; temperature-only or wavelength-independent conversion cannot establish spectral photochemistry.

title: Hydrogen peroxide UV photochemistry needs a dark and red-light control
script:
new
new
add v1 water 100mL
add v1 H2O2 0.001mol
seal v1 100mL
add v2 water 100mL
add v2 H2O2 0.001mol
seal v2 100mL
add v3 water 100mL
add v3 H2O2 0.001mol
seal v3 100mL
irradiate v1 254nm 10W/m2
irradiate v2 700nm 10W/m2
wait 60s
inspect v1
inspect v2
inspect v3
measure v1 pressure
measure v2 pressure
measure v3 pressure
measure v1 thermometer
explain v1
inspect
physical_expectation: H2O2 absorbs short-wave UV and can cleave its O–O bond into radicals. Red light is not equivalent at equal irradiance. Stable gas yield also depends on radical recombination and secondary chemistry; dark decomposition is a separate baseline.
assessment_criteria: Inspect peroxide loss and radical/stable-product coverage separately;254nm behavior should differ from red/dark if a photochemical absorption model is claimed.
Do not require a guessed universal O2 quantum yield. Any O2 yield must preserve peroxide/water oxygen and disclose modeled pathways.
Red or dark background reaction is allowed only through its own thermal/catalytic model; equal conversion solely because lamp power matches fails a spectral claim.

script:

seal v1 100mL

inspect v1

measure v1 thermometer
measure v2 thermometer
measure v1 pressure
measure v2 pressure

physical_expectation: Zero irradiance supplies zero photons and zero radiative energy. Matching otherwise-identical dark vessels must not diverge because a lamp operator was called.

Matching dark inventories should agree within numerical conservation precision; any background chemistry must act consistently on both.
A zero-flux refusal must be atomic. A wavelength-only reaction trigger despite zero photon flux fails.

title: Water-rich esterification is not compulsory complete conversion
script:
new
add v1 water 10mL
add v1 ethanol 0.01mol
add v1 acetic_acid 0.01mol
add v1 H2SO4 0.0001mol
add v2 water 100mL
add v2 ethanol 0.01mol
add v2 acetic_acid 0.01mol
add v2 H2SO4 0.0001mol
react v1 esterification
react v2 esterification
wait 1h
inspect v1
inspect v2
measure v1 chromatograph
measure v2 chromatograph
explain v1
inspect
physical_expectation: Acid-catalyzed ethanol/acetic-acid esterification is reversible and produces water. Water activity and dilution affect extent; applying the same exhaustive conversion to both aqueous mixtures would obscure equilibrium and kinetic scope.
assessment_criteria: Any supported ethyl-acetate amount is bounded by0.01mol and coupled1:1 to ethanol/acetic-acid consumption.

A quantitative comparison must disclose equilibrium/activity versus finite-time kinetic assumptions; the more water-rich mixture should not show greater equilibrium ester fraction without a specific explanation.
A curated transformation may be explicitly pedagogical, but it must not claim computed universal equilibrium or catalyst-independent kinetics. Unknown organic names are recorded as followups.

Mn inventory must be conserved; any dissolution/redox side reaction needs separate chemistry. A missing catalytic-rate model is a capability gap, not grounds to assert an invented rate.

title: Tollens-type silver reduction distinguishes a reducing sugar from acetone
script:
new
add v1 water 50mL
add v1 AgNO3 0.001mol
add v1 NH3 0.01mol
add v1 NaOH 0.002mol
add v1 glucose 0.0005mol
add v2 water 50mL
add v2 AgNO3 0.001mol
add v2 NH3 0.01mol
add v2 NaOH 0.002mol
add v2 acetone 0.0005mol
wait 10min
look v1
look v2
inspect v1
inspect v2
measure v1 uvvis
explain v1
inspect
physical_expectation: Ammoniacal Ag(I) oxidizes reducing glucose and can deposit Ag metal. Ordinary acetone does not give the corresponding Tollens silver-mirror reaction. Complexation/Ag2O preparation and sugar ring opening matter.
assessment_criteria: A supported selectivity model should produce greater Ag(0) in the glucose vessel than the acetone control; it must not infer silver merely from adding any organic molecule.
Ag atoms and oxidation/reduction electron counts must balance. At most0.001mol Ag can form from the stated silver feed.
Unsupported glucose, diamminesilver complexation or finite-time redox pathways must be explicit followups; an Ag2O precipitate alone is not a silver-mirror success.

title: Permanganate reduction changes its manganese endpoint with pH
script:
new
add v1 water 100mL
add v1 H2SO4 0.002mol
add v1 FeSO4 0.0005mol
add v1 KMnO4 0.0001mol
add v2 water 100mL
add v2 NaHCO3 0.005mol
add v2 FeSO4 0.0003mol
add v2 KMnO4 0.0001mol
wait 30s
look v1
look v2
measure v1 ph
measure v2 ph
inspect v1
inspect v2
explain v1
explain v2
inspect
physical_expectation: Acidic permanganate accepts5electrons per Mn to form Mn(II); a near-neutral buffered reduction commonly accepts3electrons to form MnO2. Fe(II) supplies one electron per oxidized iron, so matching different feed ratios exposes pH-sensitive redox endpoint selection.
assessment_criteria: Verify the actual pH first: if bicarbonate/iron chemistry defeats the intended neutral condition, record that outcome instead of forcing an MnO2 expectation.
For an acidic supported complete reaction,0.0001mol Mn(II) couples to0.0005mol Fe(II) oxidation; near-neutral MnO2 couples to0.0003mol Fe(II) oxidation.
Check explicit manganese oxidation state/phase and Fe electron balance, not purple color disappearance alone. A universal MnO2 or Mn(II) endpoint independent of conditions fails.
